about: What bcir-cc (the C rail of the verified C compiler, default target x86_64-linux, -I runtime/c) makes of each production unit runtime/c/MEMORY_CLASSIFICATION.txt lists: clean (R1-R18 clean), or blocked, with its first refusal, the construct it is about and the CSUB rung that lifts it. Held exact by tools/c/csub_ratchet.py (docs/research/BCIR_C_SUBSET_AUDIT_2026-11-10.md section 4).

bcir_cfront.c.construct: the verified compiler's own C rail: a hosted tool past the frontend's input bound

bcir_cpp.c.blocker: parse error: a multi-dimensional member array used as a value is not yet supported
bcir_cpp.c.construct: a multi-dimensional member array used as a value (a macro's `char params[16][64]`, decaying to the `char (*)[N]` its table holds); past it, the `#if` evaluator's recursive descent (`ce_comma` to `ce_prim`) and the recursion per `#include`, which R18 refuses by design: the unit needs explicit stacks, as `bcir_per.c` did

bcir_decoder_train.c.blocker: parse error: a call of more than 16 arguments is not supported
bcir_decoder_train.c.construct: a call of 18 arguments (`bcir_tensor_attention_backward_contract_variant_ws_pool`), past the claim graph's 16 reads (`BCIR_CALL_MAX_ARGS`, CF-CALLARGS); then threads, SIMD and bf16

bcir_emit.c.blocker: verify error: R18: recursive call cycle
bcir_emit.c.construct: the emitter's recursive descent over the schema tree (`der_write_full` and `der_write_content`, `per_node`, `jer_node`), which R18 refuses by design: the unit needs an explicit stack, as `bcir_per.c` did

bcir_make.c.construct: <sys/stat.h>'s `struct stat` and <dirent.h>'s `struct dirent`: POSIX's host interface past the C library, whose layouts differ by target; past them, a member through a pointer element (`bf->targets[i]->name`), which both rails refuse by design today (CF-IDXARROW)

bcir_tensor.c.blocker: parse error: a call of more than 16 arguments is not supported
bcir_tensor.c.construct: a call of 18 arguments (`bcir_tensor_attention_backward_contract_variant_ws_pool`'s workspace call), past the claim graph's 16 reads (`BCIR_CALL_MAX_ARGS`, CF-CALLARGS); then threads and SIMD
